notes: The numbers that belong to no single card: setup quantities, the turn's shape, the one standing economy rate and the end-game trigger. Anything PRINTED on a card lives in cards.json instead, anything printed on the island lives in island.json, and the five door actions live in workers.json.

SCHEMA VERSION 2 IS v31 (Dean, 02/09/2026, docs/design-changes-v31-2026-09-02-v1.md). The bump is not cosmetic: the file lost seven keys in one edit and every one of them was a coin. If you are reading a v31 number against a report written before 02/09/2026, stop - the reference was re-cut as reference-v10 and no historical number in reports/ is comparable.

THERE ARE NO COINS. Not zero coins: no coin. Nothing is earned in them, nothing is priced in them, there is no coin tie-break and there is no coin knob. What went with the currency, in one list so nobody re-derives it from an old doc: startingCoins, upgradeCostCoins (there are no starter upgrades at all now), coinPityDivisor, visitPayout in all four of its branches, giftDiscardCoins, buyCost (the card buy) and marketCost (buy at market). Six of those seven were already null or already deleted in spirit by 19/08/2026; the seventh, the upgrade price, went with the upgraded faces. The design reason is the standing finding the market note used to carry, taken all the way: money is what buys SOLITAIRE in this game, because a visit is bought with a card and every other bonus option was bought with a coin, so a coin sink in the bonus slot crowds the visit out all game. Deleting the currency deletes the competitor. The 30 Power and Endgame cards now cost 2 cards of their OWN suit, and card text that read GBP 2 or GBP 1 reads Draw 1.

THE TURN, in the order it is played (the meeple loop, Dean 04/09/2026): (1) ONE core action - Draw, Build, Grow, Harvest, Deliver; (2) ONE bonus option, either VISIT (place one meeple from your supply in the colour slot of a NEIGHBOUR'S Notice Board and immediately perform that colour's plain action) or COLLECT (take every meeple off your own Notice Board into your supply, then Draw 1). WHAT THIS DELETED FROM v31, and none of it is dormant - it is gated off and reachable only through overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json: the turn-start meeple phase (spend any number of meeples, one at a time, each leaving the game for good), the standalone free Draw 1, the card fee on a visit, and the self-visit. A meeple is now spent in the bonus slot and only there, one a turn, and a spent meeple is never removed from the game - it moves onto the neighbour's board and comes home to them on their Collect. That is the loop the design is named for, and it is also the denial: while it sits there, that colour of that neighbour is shut to the whole table. THE WILD SPEND: any TWO meeples from your supply may be spent as one of any colour, both landing in the slot bought.

baseDraw IS 2 SEE, 2 KEEP - the plain Draw action keeps BOTH cards and discards nothing. It was 2-see-1-keep from v13 until v31. The reason for the change is not generosity, it is that the discard was the last piece of hidden bookkeeping in the core five actions and it bought nothing measurable; the game's clock is now the card supply and the end trigger, not a per-draw tax. NOTE THE INTERACTION WITH THE BONUS SLOT, which changed on 04/09/2026 and changed in the game's favour: the standalone free Draw 1 is gone, so the only card the bonus slot can buy is the one attached to COLLECT. A seat taking Draw as its action and Collect as its bonus still nets 3 cards a turn with no interaction at all - collecting an EMPTY board is legal and reads as a bare Draw 1 - so the solitaire line survived the deletion with a haircut rather than a burial. Measured: it took 54.2% of turns against the v31 free Draw 1's 67.6%. That is the shape action inflation shows up in first, and it is the number the bonus mix has to keep counting separately from a Collect that actually took meeples back.

THE HAND LIMIT IS BACK, AT A FLAT 7 (12 on the day it was reinstated, cut to 7 the same day for runtime), AND IT IS A GAME RULE RATHER THAN A CARD VALUE (Dean, 02/09/2026, reversing one v31 change on evidence). WHAT THE DELETION MEASURED, because this is the number that decided it: v31 removed the limit and the first simulator run after it found the deletion had quietly removed the bound on the LEGAL-MOVE ENUMERATOR as well. The comment over `subsets` in packages/engine/src/actions.ts read 'hands are 6-8', and that bound WAS the hand limit - nothing else in the game was holding it. With hands reaching 34 cards a 2-seat position offered 43,879 legal moves, 43,845 of them build payments, because C(33,4) is 40,920 ways to pay for ONE buildable card; a re-measurement on 02/09/2026 at n=4 games found a worse position still at 116,535. A 2-seat game went from about 0.1 seconds to 1-15 minutes, so the watch-list suite could only be run at n=8 and every conclusion from that run is an anecdote. The bots hoarded to a median hand of 18, the free bonus Draw 1 became strictly dominant (beating a neighbour visit 3:1, failing the hook assertion) and the 2-seat game ran to 45 rounds. IT IS A DESIGN FAILURE BEFORE IT IS AN ENGINEERING ONE: a gateway player choosing between forty thousand ways to pay for one build is not a shippable turn, and diminishing returns on a card in hand are what make a neighbour worth visiting at all. THE SHAPE OF THE RESTORED RULE IS NOT THE OLD ONE. It is ONE GLOBAL NUMBER, not five printed per-suit ones - the Barn still prints nothing and stays blank, because this belongs on the player aid where a rule that applies to everybody belongs. It is checked at the END of your turn only; you may exceed it mid-turn, which is how several cards work (O14 sows a whole hand, W10 empties one into the barn) and is the old rule kept deliberately. Overflow discards down to the limit at the turn boundary. 12 IS A GUESS AND A KNOB: it is roughly three turns of accumulation above the 4-card opening hand, generous enough that the limit is a brake rather than a clock, and overlays/hand-limit-10.overlay.json and overlays/hand-limit-15.overlay.json are the paired arms, and overlays/hand-limit.sweep.json is the full ladder. null disables the rule and restores the v31 behaviour, which is the control arm nobody should run without reading the numbers above first.

bonusDraw IS NO LONGER A BONUS OPTION OF ITS OWN (04/09/2026). The number survives and is read in one place only: it is how many cards COLLECT draws after sweeping your board. Under overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json it goes back to being the standalone free Draw 1, taken instead of visiting a Notice Board, and the yardstick every door had to beat - which is what made the Orchard door a Draw 3 rather than a Draw 2 under those rules, because a door handing back 2 cards for the 1 card you placed was worth exactly the free option. THAT WHOLE ARGUMENT HAS NO SUBJECT UNDER THE SHIPPED RULES: a visit costs no card, so there is nothing to cancel, and the free option is gone, so there is nothing to be worse than. The Orchard door is a plain Draw 2 and the door set has no exception left in it. Raising this number is still the cheapest way to make the solitaire line beat every door in the game at once, and it is the lever Dean declined to sweep on 03/09/2026; it now carries a meeple sweep with it, so it is no longer a pure solitaire dial.

selfVisitAllowed IS DEAD UNDER THE SHIPPED RULES AND IS READ ONLY BY THE CONTROL. It was risk 2 of the v31 pass, armed on purpose: you could place your bonus card on your OWN Notice Board and take your own suit's action, with the only brake being that your card counted toward your own threshold and shut your own door. IT MEASURED AT ABOUT 22% OF TURNS and the meeple loop deletes it outright (rule X5: there is no self-visit under any flag, and the enumerator refuses one whatever this key says). The risk it named did not go away, it changed defendant: the free Draw 1 ate the slot, not the self-visit, and the empty-board COLLECT is what inherited the job. a08-the-hook must still count a self-visit separately and must still never credit one as interaction - under the shipped rules it should assert the line reads exactly 0, which is a claim worth failing on rather than an assumption. Set true or false as you like here; only overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json makes it mean anything.

bonusTiming (Dean, 03/09/2026 - A CORRECTION, NOT AN EXPERIMENT): the turn is meeples, then your CORE ACTION, then the bonus option. This engine and both design docs had carried the opposite order since 19/08/2026 ('start': bonus before the action) and were simply wrong about the game. 'start' survives as the paired control (overlays/bonus-first.overlay.json) and 'any' as v14's once-per-turn-any-point (overlays/bonus-any-time.overlay.json). THE THREE ARE NOT ORDERABLE BY POWER: under 'start' a door can fuel the action that follows it, under 'end' the action can set the door up - fill a building then Harvest it through the Wheat door, harvest into the barn then Deliver through the Vegetable one - so expect the DOOR MIX to move and not only the visit rate. SLOT UNSPENT still reads the window, but its absolute is the rational floor and only the delta between arms means anything.

visitCurrency IS meeple AND THAT IS THE GAME (Dean ruled it in 04/09/2026; docs/meeple-loop-visit-handoff-2026-09-04-v1.md is the design, docs/meeple-loop-measurement-2026-09-04-v1.md is what it measured). A visit costs a MEEPLE placed in the colour slot of a NEIGHBOUR's Notice Board, never your own; the Notice Board is not a building at all - no threshold, no stack, no sow, no harvest, no clog - and the bonus slot's other half is COLLECT. card is the v31 game and is now the CONTROL, at overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json: a card fee onto a board that is a building with a threshold of 2, self-visiting legal, a standalone free Draw 1, the turn-start meeple spend, the Orchard door at Draw 3 and a meeple on both delivery spaces of every tile. WHAT meeple IGNORES: selfVisitAllowed and economy.noticeBoardThreshold. bonusTiming, bonusSlotsPerTurn and handLimit all still apply and are unchanged. IT WAS RULED IN ON A MEASUREMENT THAT WAS NOT FLATTERING, and pretending otherwise would make the next reader mistrust this file. The hook FELL, 0.41 to 0.37 rival visits per player per turn, and the game got 35-43% LONGER. It was ruled in on the two things that did move: the two dead meeple colours came back to life (Apiary and Dairy take 46% of door uses against 32%, and the door-mix assertion goes FAIL to PASS), self-visiting became impossible by construction, and interaction per GAME rose 21% even as interaction per turn fell. Whether the hook is a per-turn or a per-game quantity is a design decision nobody has made. NO NUMBER FROM BEFORE THIS IS COMPARABLE: the reference is re-cut as reference-v12.

startingMeeplesPerColour AND meepleCapPerColour ARE THE ECONOMY'S TWO NUMBERS, and both are read only under visitCurrency meeple (rules R3 and R4). Every player starts with ONE meeple of each of the five colours, NOT drawn from the island bag, so the loop is primed before anybody delivers and a first-turn visit is possible at every seat. THE STARTING FIVE ARE THE IGNITION, NOT AN ACCELERANT: the arm with none reads a hook of 0.09 and an empty-board Collect on 87% of turns, which is the solitaire draw engine v31 already was, only slower. THE CAP IS 2 AS OF 05/09/2026, AND THAT IS A CHANGE OF RULING THAT ARRIVED AS A PASSENGER, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WRITTEN OUT HERE. It was 1 from 04/09/2026, ruled by Dean AGAINST its own measurement on teach simplicity: 'you may never hold two of a colour' is one sentence and a visible rule, and the sweep that said cap 2 reads a hook of 0.40 against 0.37 and boxes 7.67 meeples a game against 13.41 was in front of him when he ruled it. The amended R4 (cap 2) was then built into the handoff v2 arm and carried into R17, and on 05/09/2026 Dean ruled R17 in AS MEASURED, so the cap moved to 2 with it. ⚠️ NOBODY HAS RE-ARGUED THE TEACH COST: the 04/09 ruling was about what a player can hold in their head, and ruling in an arm does not answer that. Under R17 the cap has also largely stopped doing design work - it boxes 1.14 meeples a game against 13.45 under the v1 loop - so the case for 1 is now almost purely the teach case. The v1 rule is one flag away at overlays/meeple-loop-v1.overlay.json, and the cap sweeps under R17 are overlays/meeple-on-board-cap-one-v1.overlay.json and -cap-three-. THE COMPONENT COUNT FOLLOWS FROM THESE TWO AND IS DEAN'S QUESTION, NOT THE ENGINE'S, AND THE CAP CHANGE MAKES IT WORSE: at a cap of 2 a seat can hold up to 10 meeples rather than 5, so five per player plus one per tile is a floor and not a count. The printed bag is 25. The bag is unchanged here, because the sim never needed it to grow: the starting meeples are not drawn from it.

meepleAsCard IS R15 (Dean, 04/09/2026 evening, docs/meeple-loop-visit-handoff-2026-09-04-v2.md), AND SINCE 05/09/2026 IT DEFAULTS true: it is the shipped game. Wherever a rule asks you to pay or spend a card, a meeple of the matching colour may pay it instead - build costs including the n-of-suit requirements and the 'any' slots, the 2-own-suit cost on Power and Endgame cards, a Grow's activation payment, and a delivery crate. It is NOT a Sow, because a Sow is a placement and a meeple is not a card to place, and it is NOT a balloon move cost (C62, a default rather than a ruling). R10's wild pair is reused rather than re-rated: two meeples of any colours are one card of any colour, at the same rate they are one meeple of any colour. A meeple never counts toward the hand limit, because it is never in a hand. A meeple paid into a Grow never joins the stack and never counts toward the threshold, so IT CAN ACTIVATE A BUILDING ALREADY AT ITS THRESHOLD - a priced clog bypass, Dean's ruling of 04/09/2026, and the one thing R15 does that a card never could. ⭐ WHERE THE MEEPLE GOES IS NOT THIS KNOB, IT IS meepleAsCardGoesTo, AND UNDER R15 ALONE THE ANSWER WAS THE BOX AND THAT KILLED THE LOOP: see the R17 note below. false is the v1 loop of 04/09/2026, where a meeple only ever performs its colour's action through a neighbour's board and is never a payment; it survives as overlays/meeple-loop-v1.overlay.json, which is now a real arm again rather than the no-op it was for a day.

slotToll IS THE AMENDED R6 (Dean, 04/09/2026 evening), AND SINCE 05/09/2026 IT DEFAULTS 1: A NOTICE BOARD SLOT IS PRICED, NOT BLOCKED. Nothing is ever refused. Visiting a slot that already holds k meeples costs 1 times k EXTRA meeples of ANY colours on top of the acting meeple, and every one of those extra meeples - the toll - goes STRAIGHT TO THE BOX, never to the host. So a slot already holding two meeples costs three to visit: one joins the slot as normal, two are boxed. A wild pair sitting in a slot counts as two occupants, not one. ⚠️ THE TOLL IS A SINK, NOT A PAYMENT TO THE HOST. Dean's own framing is that it 'might be a good way of sinking surplus meeples' under the amended cap of 2, so read it beside meepleCapPerColour and never alone, and read it beside paymentSlotToll, which is the SEPARATE and FLAT toll a payment placement pays. Under R17 the toll is the main drain left: 57.5% of the 12.16 meeples leaving the game each game is toll. null is the v1 rule - a slot holding any meeple is BLOCKED and refuses that colour outright until the owner Collects - and it survives in overlays/meeple-loop-v1.overlay.json and in the v31 control.

⭐ meepleAsCardGoesTo, paymentSlotToll AND paymentHostChoice ARE R17 (Dean, 05/09/2026), THE CHANGE THAT MADE THE MEEPLE ECONOMY A LOOP RATHER THAN A DRAIN, AND THE REASON THIS FILE'S DEFAULTS MOVED. Read all three only under meepleAsCard true. A meeple spent as a card is PLACED ON ANOTHER PLAYER'S NOTICE BOARD, in its own colour's slot, exactly as a visit places one, and the host takes it back on their Collect. ⛔ IT BUYS THE PAYER NOTHING ELSE: no door action, it is not a visit, and the bonus slot is untouched. The WHOLE payment goes to ONE chosen host (paymentHostChoice perPayment; perMeeple was Dean's first ruling the same day and was ruled back on the branching factor, 25,827 ways to buy one building at four seats against 4,063). Landing on a slot that already holds a meeple costs ONE FLAT extra meeple of any colour, to the box, however deep the slot (paymentSlotToll 1), and that flatness is the one place it differs from slotToll. WHY IT EXISTS: under 'box' the resource use ATE the loop - meeples left the game 18.27 times a game against 9.44 visits, median supply in the last third hit 0.0, and the hook collapsed 0.35 to 0.09. Placing them instead recovered the hook to 0.31 and produced the closest thing to a level bonus slot this project has measured: rival visit 30.9% of turns against the largest solitaire line's 31.9%, a gap of ONE point where every previous version sat 21 to 75 points apart. It also SHORTENED the game (3p 35.4 to 26.5 rounds). ⚠️ IT WAS RULED IN WITH THREE COSTS ON THE TABLE, recorded here so nobody reads the flip as free: 2-player blocked-want tripled 1.2% to 7.7% (C65, which reopens C57 and Dean's island alternative X2), the barn glut DOUBLED +0.5 to +1.0 and is the first movement in that number across four arms (C66), and the balance suite runs 2.6x slower. 'box' is the handoff v2 arm and survives as overlays/meeple-as-card-v1.overlay.json, which is now the control for R17.

SETUP IS FOUR CARDS AND NOTHING ELSE. startingHand is 4 from your own suit deck, startingBarnCards is 0, and there are no coins to start with. The barn starts EMPTY, which is new: it used to be seeded with 1 card. The barn is now purely a place to store cards ready for delivery and PRINTS NOTHING - and that survives the hand limit coming back, because the limit is no longer a card value. See turn.handLimit below.

noticeBoardThreshold IS READ ONLY BY THE v31 CONTROL (04/09/2026). Under the shipped rules the Notice Board is not a building: query.thresholdOf returns null for it, which makes isFull false, canTakeCard false and roomOn 0, so it falls out of the sow targets, the harvest targets, the Apiary door's legality check and A21 The Wax Hall's count all at once, and nothing can ever be placed on it. What blocks a door now is a MEEPLE IN A SLOT, one colour at a time, cleared by the owner's Collect rather than by a Harvest - and it measured far gentler than the old clog: the blocked-want rate at 2 players is 1.3%, and no seat ever had all five slots blocked, at any seat count. THE HISTORY IS WORTH KEEPING because it is the only lever ever measured to move the suit balance, and it was monotone across three paired n=1580 arms on the older two-building surface: at t=4 Orchard won 80.8%, at t=3 62.8%, at t=2 42.0% against an even share of 36.4%. On the later single-door surface at n=500: t=5 clogged 2.3% of turn boundaries, t=3 5%, t=2 11%, with the suit spread most even at 2. Dean's reading of why a loose door is worse than it looks: 'you get to use other players cards a lot, but that number also decreases how often you can harvest and make use of the cards people give you, making it more valuable to the visitor rather than the person who is visited.' Never raise it without re-running the suite against the control, which is the only arm it now moves.

endGame.trigger is deliveryCount (Dean, 2026-08-09, with the flat island) and survives v31 untouched in its wording and at risk in its number. The game ends when any ONE seat completes its deliveriesToTrigger-th ISLAND delivery, after which every other player takes furtherTurnsEach more turns. Balloon moves are Deliver actions but not island deliveries, so they never count. It is still one observable trigger read off public state - a receipt count in front of a player - and still a thing a player does rather than a deck running out. It is FLAT at every seat count, so 6 is half the 2-seat island's 12 delivery spaces, a third of the 3-seat island's 18 and a quarter of the 4-seat island's 24; that asymmetry is known and taken, and 2p is where to watch it. WHY IT IS NOW THE FIRST KNOB TO SWEEP, AND THE REASON HAS REVERSED. v31's forecast was a SHORTER game: the bonus slot bought a whole core action for one card and meeples added uncapped free ones. Measured, it ran LONGER, and the meeple loop then added 35-43% on top of that (2p 32.8 rounds, 3p 31.6, 4p 30.3 against 27.6 / 23.4 / 21.2). Actions per turn FELL, 2.39 to 2.21, while turns rose - the arm buys fewer actions per turn and needs more turns to reach the same island. Against a 40-60 minute gateway target that is the most serious open number in the game, and this is the knob that moves it. overlays/end-trigger-8.overlay.json is the paired arm; overlays/end-trigger.sweep.json is the full ladder.
unresolved: GAME LENGTH IS THE OPEN NUMBER (04/09/2026). The meeple loop measured 35-43% longer than v31 - 2p 32.8 rounds, 3p 31.6, 4p 30.3 - and v31 was already longer than v30. Nothing has been dialled for it. endGame.deliveriesToTrigger is the knob and overlays/end-trigger.sweep.json is the ladder; nobody has run it against the shipped rules.

THE HOOK, AND WHETHER IT IS A PER-TURN OR A PER-GAME QUANTITY. The meeple loop reads 0.37 rival visits per player per turn against v31's 0.41 and a floor of 0.5, while rival visits PER GAME rose 21%, from 28.7 to 34.8. Both are true and they point opposite ways. Until somebody decides which the floor is stated against, a08-the-hook is measuring a quantity nobody has defined.

THE EMPTY-BOARD COLLECT IS THE FREE DRAW 1 WEARING A HAT. It takes 54.2% of turns against the rival visit's 36.8%. The design deleted the standalone Draw 1 and then re-attached a Draw 1 to the option that is legal on almost every turn, so the solitaire line survived the deletion with a 13-point haircut. rules.turn.bonusDraw is the dial and it has never been swept.

THE MEEPLE CAP IS 1 AGAINST A MEASUREMENT THAT PREFERS 2 (hook 0.40 against 0.37, waste 7.67 boxed a game against 13.41). Ruled by Dean on 04/09/2026 for teach simplicity, knowingly. It is recorded as a live trade-off rather than as a settled number; the arms are overlays/meeple-loop-cap-two-v1.overlay.json and -cap-three-.

THE BOT HOARDING DIAL IS STILL UNMEASURED AND STILL NOT OVERLAY-ADDRESSABLE. meepleGain (2.5) and MEEPLE_LATENT (0.4) were set by argument. Under v31 they priced one faucet and one drain; they now price the visit, the Collect, the cap and the island, which is most of the bonus slot. The cap result in particular is partly a sweep of the bots' opinion of what a stored meeple is worth. Exposing them as knobs is a code change nobody has made.
THE VEGETABLE DOOR COLLAPSED, 18% of door uses to 7%. Deliver is the scoring action and its colour is now the least visited on the table. Nobody has looked at why.
THE BARN GLUT IS UNTOUCHED at +0.5 on both arms, despite about 29 fee cards a game no longer flowing into barns through the old boards.

THE MONOCULTURE PULL (v31 risk 3). The Farmstead pays 1 VP per own-suit card built and the Power and Endgame cards cost 2 cards of their own suit. The own-crop build share was 82.6% before and 83.3% after. Neither pull is a knob; undoing either is a card change.

THE INTERFACE HAS NOT BEEN PORTED. packages/ui pins itself to overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json and draws the v31 game: the Notice Board as a building with a fill bar, a visit assembled by dragging a card, no colour slots and no wild pair. See the docblock on `data` in packages/ui/src/session/table.ts for what the pass owes.
The 2-seat game is still the seat count with the least evidence behind it. deliveriesToTrigger is flat, the island is half-used at 12 spaces, and nothing here has ever been played by a human.
